source_text.body:
Turn tagged Readwise articles into Notion summaries
A Zapier Agent reads an article in Readwise Reader, reviews the user's highlights, and drafts a summary into a Notion database when a specific tag is applied.
·
Jan 30, 2025
Done with
ZA
Zapier Agents
What they did
They first store all Readwise highlights in a Zapier Table. When they add a specific tag to an article in Readwise Reader, a Zapier Agent reads the article, reviews those highlights, and drafts a summary into a Notion database; the person then reviews it, writes the full post, and updates a property to queue publishing.
How it went
The summaries were described as pretty good. They improved them by giving the agent a Notion page as a knowledge source with guidance on writing style and tone, but the human still finished the post manually.
Worth knowing
The main catch is setup complexity: they used both Readwise’s native integration and a custom integration for actions the native one did not support.
Try it yourself
with
Zapier Agents
Copy prompt
Create a Zapier Agent that triggers when I add the tag [tag name] to an article in Readwise Reader. It should read the article and my highlights, then draft a summary of [length] that reflects the points I highlighted and add it to my Notion database [database name]. Include the title, link and tags in the Notion entry. You're done when a test article with the tag produces a correct Notion page, and show me the draft before the first save.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/zapier/comments/1qj0yen/whats_the_most_creative_thing_youve_automated
